findings.current:
“How curious. The martial artists I know will drink without a second thought, but they don’t usually smoke opium.”

“Opium?”
findings.defect: Hong Jin names poppy, not opium. Naming opium in both lines gives away the realization Taekyung has only after hearing the explanation.
findings.rationale: 앵속 means poppy; Taekyung identifies its dried sap as opium in the following beat.
findings.replacement:
“How curious. The martial artists I know drink readily enough, but they rarely touch poppy.”

“Poppy…?”
findings.source:
“희한하네. 내가 아는 무인들은 술은 곧잘 마셔도 앵속(罌粟)은 잘 안 하던데.”

“앵속이라면…….”

findings.current: *Opium. No, that distinctive scent of the opium Hong Jin calls yingsu… I’ve smelled it before. And much stronger than this.*
findings.defect: The thought equates Hong Jin’s word for poppy with opium and adds an unnecessary romanization.
findings.rationale: Taekyung corrects his own thought from 아편 to 앵속 and recalls a stronger instance of the scent.
findings.replacement: *Opium. No, that distinctive scent of poppy… I’ve smelled it before. Stronger than Hong Jin’s.*
findings.source: ‘아편. 아니 앵속의 그 독특한 향…… 이미 맡아 본 적이 있어. 홍진의 것보다도 더욱 진하게.’

findings.current:
*“What? The Blue Opium War?”*

*“The Blue Opium… Hey, class president! Kim Minjeong!”*

*“Yes?”*

*“Call the cops right now. I’m going to beat this punk and get arrested for assaulting a student.”*
findings.defect: “Blue Opium” invents a different mistake and loses the Korean joke’s reference to child-and-youth sex-crime protections.
findings.rationale: 아청 is the source’s mistaken word, not a color or a kind of opium. The brief note preserves the reference without making the spoken line more explicit than the Korean.
findings.replacement:
*“What? The Youth Protection War?[^1]”*

*“Youth Protection… Hey, class president! Kim Minjeong!”*

*“Yes?”*

*“Call the cops right now. I’m going to beat this punk and get arrested for assaulting a student.”*

[^1]: Taekyung mishears *apyeon* (opium) as *acheong*, shorthand associated with Korea’s law protecting children and youth from sexual crimes.
findings.source:
‘아청 전쟁이요?’

‘아청…… 야, 반장아. 김민정이.’

‘네?’

‘지금 바로 경찰 불러라. 그냥 내 오늘 점마 조지고 폭력 교사로 잡혀 들어갈란다.’

findings.current: the white-skinned islander bastards invaded the real mainland bastards.
findings.defect: “Bastards” softens and changes the repeated ethnic slur that carries Taekyung’s crude account of the Opium War.
findings.rationale: The narrator applies 짱깨 first to the white-skinned islanders and then to the mainlanders; the repetition and offensiveness are intentional.
findings.replacement: the white-skinned island chinks invaded the genuine mainland chinks.
findings.source: 흰 피부의 섬나라 짱깨가 진또배기 대륙 짱깨를 침략했다는 사실

findings.defect: Dropping 마 makes Taekyung’s answer an incomplete repetition of what the teacher actually shouted.
findings.rationale: He repeats the teacher’s opening “마! 진태경!” instead of recalling the lesson.

findings.current: *Right. The day we returned from meeting the Emperor.*
findings.defect: The draft drops “immediately after” and supplies an unsupported “we.”
findings.rationale: 직후 pins the remembered scent to the period immediately after the audience; the thought does not specify a group returning.
findings.replacement: *Right. Immediately after I returned from my audience with the Emperor. That very day.*
findings.source: ‘그래, 황제를 알현하고 돌아온 직후. 바로 그날이었어.’

findings.defect: “Is that right?” reads as a request to verify the time rather than Taekyung’s incredulous reaction.
findings.rationale: 이거 맞냐 is a colloquial expression of disbelief here, not a literal request for confirmation.
findings.replacement: “Five hours late. Are you kidding me?”

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, but it names opium before Taekyung’s realization, changes a classroom joke, and softens a pointed slur.
